Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our SOC2 team is consolidating the encryption artifacts for the audit packet and had a couple of quick clarifying questions about Redwood's KMS/HSM practices before we pull your evidence into the consolidated binder: 

1) Rotation window: can you confirm the SLA for rotating tenant KEKs when an emergency rekey is initiated? Our policy expects emergency rotations to complete (rollout + verification) within 48 hours and we need to map vendor timelines. Do you have documented service-level timelines or an operational playbook excerpt we can reference?

2) Retention of retired keys: for tenant-byok scenarios, what is Redwood's default retention window for encrypted key artifacts/keystore snapshots after rotation? Is there an option to shorten/extend this per contract?

3) HSM attestation: for on-prem and customer-managed HSMs, do you provide an attestation PDF or signed statement of custody/firmware version at the time of the audit snapshot? If so, a sample would be helpful.

4) Sampling artifacts: would Redwood be able to provide a small sample (anonymized) of the keystore-index file and rotation snapshot (checksums only) so our auditors can validate the chain-of-custody workflow without seeing tenant secrets?

If it's easier, feel free to send a single archive with redacted artifacts and a short narrative describing each file. We need this by EOD Monday 2026-10-18 to include it in the audit deliverable.

Best,

Leah — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments and next steps below.

1) Emergency rotation SLA: our operational playbook defines an emergency rekey response goal of 24–48 hours end-to-end for tenant KEK rotations (detection -> rotation -> verification). For Dedicated and Private customers with a reserved SLA we commit to the lower bound (24h) as part of the change control. I can paste the relevant excerpt from the runbook.

2) Retention of retired keys: by default we retain rotation snapshots and keystore indices for 90 days. For Private deployments or contract amendments we can extend retention up to 2 years; we also support shorter retention on request (minimum 30 days) for customers who need more aggressive purging.

3) HSM attestation: for hosted HSMs we provide the vendor attestation bundle (FIPS/HSM firmware) and an internal custody statement. For customer-managed HSMs we accept the vendor-provided attestation and store that artifact alongside the rotation snapshot; we can provide a redacted sample.

4) Sampling artifacts: yes — attached is a small anonymized sample set (checksums only, no key material) and an index mapping that explains the fields auditors typically check.

Attachments: rotation-snapshot-20261015.tar.gz (checksums only), keystore-audit-index.csv, hsm-attestation-2025.pdf

Next steps: Marissa (security ops) will export a couple of runbook excerpts and a short narrative describing our verification steps for the auditors. Jonas is copied for the operational timeline confirmation and to confirm the 24h emergency SLA for Dedicated customers. If that timeline works, we'll upload the archive to the shared drive and send a HubSpot link. Expect the runbook excerpt by EOD today.

Hi Leah — forwarding the runbook excerpt and a short verification checklist as promised. I've redacted customer identifiers and replaced raw blobs with checksums and file size metadata. Below are the verification steps our auditors run locally when they receive the archive: 

- Verify envelope: confirm the rotation snapshot archive contains the keystore-index.csv and a signed manifest (manifest.sig) created by our rotation service.
- Check timestamps: ensure rotation start/finish timestamps fall within the claimed window; we include millisecond-precision event logs.
- Validate checksums: keystore entries in the index are matched to checksums listed in the snapshot (SHA256).
- HSM attestation: review the attestation PDF for firmware version, HSM serial (redacted), and operator witness statement.
